newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Eni and Enel sign electricity deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Eni and Enel sign electricity deal.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled energy giant Eni and electricity utility Enel have signed a letter of intent opening the way for the creation of a joint venture to produce electricity, the firms said in a statement on Monday.
The two Italian giants said they expected to set up the company in 1997 and wanted it to be listed on the major international stock exchanges.
"The joint initiative should be seen as an independent, non-subsidised electricity firm also capable of competing at an international level," the statement said.

It said the firm would have initial output capacity of 5,000 megawatts -- around a third of Italy's free market needs. It would be generated by centres close to Enel generators and Eni's refinery and petrochemical plants.

"(The) technology will allow production at very competitive costs with limited emissions to the atmosphere, thus contributing to energy savings for the country whilst at the same time safeguarding the environment," the statement said.
Eni said that by outsourcing its own production capacity, it hoped to cut down on its own electricity costs.

Eni managing director Franco Bernabei was quoted as saying at the weekend that Eni's goal was not to simply to enter the electric energy business "which in Italy is a saturated market" but to be able to supply the Eni group's oil refineries and chemical plants "with energy at a highly competitive cost." -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
